cover.headline: The heavy lifting is done; now five launches have to earn back the dilution
cover.lead: Biocon is India's biosimilars champion: copies of insulins and cancer and immunology antibodies sold in 120 countries, 61% of FY26 revenue, plus a small generics arm and 52.4% of the listed research firm Syngene. In FY26 it bought out every minority partner in Biocon Biologics and retired its structured debt, so from 29-Jun-2026 it owns 100% of its main business and pays ~₹300 cr a year less interest; the price was 43 cr new shares (+36%). The street values Biocon on a **sum of the parts**. Ours: biosimilars at **21x Sep-28E EBITDA** (Biocon's own look-through forward multiple since FY24, 19.4x, × the +7.46% pharma factor), generics at 9.5x (Aurobindo's history × the same factor), Syngene and Bicara at market less 20%, less ₹9,193 cr of net debt: **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with BUY.** Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}, bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}. Our EPS (₹3.9 / ₹7.5 / ₹10.6 for FY27-29E) is below the street, and both cross-checks sit below the target: this is a call on biosimilar value, not on near-term earnings.

arguments.h: A real biosimilars franchise entering its launch year
arguments.p: Biosimilars EBITDA before other income rose from ₹1,900 cr in FY25 to ₹2,566 cr in FY26 (24.7% margin). FY27 brings five growth products in the US and Europe: aflibercept (Yesafili, US launch Aug-2026, interchangeable), denosumab (US launch Apr-2026), insulin aspart (moving to commercial US channels), ustekinumab and bevacizumab, plus a second insulin line in Malaysia. Old products hold up: US pegfilgrastim and trastuzumab still have 23-25% shares years after launch. We forecast biosimilars EBITDA of ₹3,568 cr in FY28E.

arguments.h: The structure is finally simple, and the debt is falling
arguments.p: No more minorities in BBL, no more structured instruments, one board. Interest fell 23% YoY to ₹213 cr in Q1FY27. On our numbers net debt falls from ₹10,461 cr (Mar-26, 3.0x EBITDA) to ₹7,669 cr by Mar-28 (1.7x), because capex is past its peak and free cash goes to debt. The cost: shares went from 120 cr to 163 cr in a year, so FY28E EPS of ₹7.5 is still below FY24's reported ₹8.5.

arguments.h: But the rest of the group is a drag, and the second half has to deliver
arguments.p: Q1FY27 biosimilars grew 16% in rupees but only ~5% in constant currency; generics made 1.5% EBITDA margin in FY26 (before other income) despite new plants; Syngene's revenue fell 16% after a big client cut orders. Management has promised a stronger second half before. Our FY27E EBITDA of ₹3,767 cr needs ~₹970 cr a quarter in Q2-Q4 vs ₹847 cr in Q1. We are 11% below MOSL on FY28E EPS (₹7.5 vs ₹8.4).

arguments.h: Valuation: the SOTP says cheap, the cross-checks say fair
arguments.p: At ₹370 the market pays ~18.2x forward EBITDA for the biosimilars business on our look-through, below its 19.4x median since FY24 and below the street's 20-22x. Our SOTP gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}. On P/E the stock is expensive (40.9x Sep-28E EPS), and consolidated EV/EBITDA (₹407) and the DCF (₹412, ₹369 after Syngene's minorities) sit near the price. The upside needs the biosimilar multiple to hold while EBITDA grows ~15% a year.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): the first test of the promised second-half acceleration (the first weeks of aflibercept, the Malaysia line, generics margins, Syngene).
US payer contracts for calendar 2027 (negotiated July-September each year): formulary positions for aspart, ustekinumab, denosumab and aflibercept.
FDA classification of the April-2026 pre-licence inspection at Biocon Park (five procedural observations) and the pending biosimilar pertuzumab filing.
BBL's $800 mn 6.67% notes become callable from October 2026: a refinancing at a lower rate would cut interest further; rating upgrades in FY26 help.
Mylan (Viatris) owns 5.6% of Biocon and its six-month lock-up ended in July 2026: a possible block sale is an overhang.
Syngene's recovery (FY27 a "transition year", growth from FY28) and any move to monetise the Bicara stake (~₹985 cr at 30-Sep).

sections.title: Three businesses: biosimilars make the money, generics fill the plants, Syngene is a listed stake

blocks.p: Biocon has three operating businesses and a small investment. **Biosimilars** (Biocon Biologics; ₹10,380 cr of FY26 external revenue, 61%) are near-copies of biologic drugs: insulins (glargine, aspart, human insulin), cancer antibodies (trastuzumab, bevacizumab, pegfilgrastim), immunology (adalimumab, etanercept, ustekinumab), bone health (denosumab) and eye care (aflibercept). About 40% of biosimilar sales are in North America, 35% in Europe and 25% in emerging markets (CFO, Q4FY26 call). **Generics** (₹2,859 cr, 17%) are mostly APIs (60-67%: statins, immunosuppressants, peptides) plus finished pills and injectables in the US, Europe and emerging markets, incl. the GLP-1 liraglutide. **Research services** are Syngene (₹3,689 cr of external revenue, 22%), a listed contract research and manufacturing company in which Biocon owns 52.4%. Biocon also holds 5.52 mn shares (~10%) of Bicara Therapeutics, a Nasdaq-listed cancer-drug developer.

sections.title: From enzymes to biosimilars, then a debt-funded leap (Viatris) and a share-funded clean-up (FY26)

blocks.p: Biocon's history has two halves. For 40 years it was an organic builder: fermentation, then insulin, then biosimilars developed with Mylan, which sold them in the West. In 2022 it bought Mylan's (Viatris's) biosimilars business to sell its own products, and paid for it with debt and with a stake in Biocon Biologics. FY26 undid the complexity: two share issues and a share swap retired the structured debt and bought out every minority investor in BBL. The business is now simpler and less leveraged, but shareholders own a 36% smaller slice of each rupee of profit than in March 2025.

sections.title: Biosimilars: a growing, regulated, deflating market where scale and reliability matter more than science

blocks.h: What makes biosimilars different from generics

blocks.p: A biosimilar is a near-copy of a biologic drug made in living cells (insulins, antibodies). It needs a factory, a cell line and years of analytical and clinical work, so there are fewer competitors than in pill generics, and prices fall more slowly: Biocon's pegfilgrastim still has 'a fifth to a fourth' of its US market eight years after launch (Q1FY27 call).

The US is the prize and the hardest market: hospital ('medical benefit') drugs are priced on average selling prices that fall as share rises, so 'market share and ASP have always been inversely proportional' (CEO, Q4FY26 call); pharmacy drugs need formulary listings from the big benefit managers, contracted in July-September each year (Q1FY27 call).

blocks.h: The US: the prize, and the hardest market

blocks.p: Biocon puts its portfolio's total market opportunity at $200 bn+ (June-2026 investor presentation, GlobalData); slide 21 shows US addressable markets (CY2025) of ~$6 bn for aflibercept (US launch H2 CY2026), ~$5 bn bevacizumab (Oct-25), ~$7 bn denosumab (Apr-26), ~$8 bn ustekinumab (Feb-25), ~$3 bn aspart (Sep-25), ~$1 bn liraglutide (H1 CY2026) and ~$34 bn semaglutide (DMF filed) (product order as we read the slide). The US accounts for ~47% of Biocon's group revenue (AR FY26 note 40). Its biosimilars market has two channels: hospital ("Part B", medical-benefit) drugs such as oncology antibodies and denosumab, where prices are set by average selling prices and fall as competitors win share; and pharmacy drugs such as insulin, ustekinumab and adalimumab, where access depends on formularies run by three big benefit managers. Biocon's management says it prefers margin over share: "market share and ASP have always been inversely proportional" (CEO, Q4FY26 call).

blocks.p: Regulation is turning friendlier: the FDA's draft guidance waiving comparative efficacy (phase-3) studies 'reduced development cost by 50%' and cuts 3-4 years (CEO, Q4FY26 call), and interchangeability rules are being simplified. The flip side: cheaper entry invites more rivals, incl. Chinese insulin makers (Q4FY26 call). US tariffs: generics and biosimilars are exempt under current law; a presidential post threatened tariffs within two years (Q1FY27 call).

Global insulin market ~$7-8 bn, of which recombinant human insulin ~$1.5 bn and glargine/aspart ~$3 bn each; Biocon is the only biosimilar insulin maker in the US (CEO, Q4FY26 call). Biocon's generics are mostly APIs (60-67%): fermentation-based molecules (statins, immunosuppressants such as tacrolimus and mycophenolate) and peptides, where 'there is hardly any competition' in fermentation-based peptides (CEO, Q4FY26 call). Formulations are sold in the US (Cranbury, New Jersey plant), Europe and emerging markets. GLP-1s: liraglutide (Victoza/Saxenda copies) approved in the UK (first generic GLP-1 in a regulated market, 2024), the EU, Australia and the US (Q4FY26); semaglutide DMF filed, products filed in Canada and Brazil (June-2026 presentation). Many Indian companies are launching semaglutide copies where patents lapse in 2026, so GLP-1 prices will fall fast.

Syngene (NSE: SYNGENE) is a contract research, development and manufacturing company (CRDMO) for global pharma and biotech. FY27 is a 'transition year' after lower offtake from one large biologics client; revenue -16% in Q1FY27, 12% operating margin; return to growth from FY28 (Q1FY27 call). Its share price fell from ~₹700 in 2024 to ₹365.3 on 30-Sep-2026 (Screener).

blocks.callout: **So what:** biosimilars are a better business than pill generics (fewer rivals, slower price falls, sticky hospital contracts) but not a monopoly: every big molecule now has five to ten biosimilars, and the FDA is making entry cheaper. The winners will be the companies that make reliably at low cost and launch early; Biocon is one of a handful with the scale to do both.

blocks.p: The volume tailwind is real: biosimilar revenue grew from ₹8,818 cr in FY24 to ₹10,380 cr in FY26 and we forecast ₹15,095 cr in FY29E (65.2% of revenue). The price tailwind is not: management tells investors to "budget for some erosion" (CFO, Q4FY26) and will not chase share at the expense of margin. And the per-share tailwind has been absorbed by the capital structure (see History).

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** the sector tailwind reaches Biocon's revenue and EBITDA; whether it reaches the shareholder depends on margins in the US launches and on debt repayment, both of which only start to show from the second half of FY27.

sections.title: Biosimilars: twelve products, five launches, and a margin that has to hold through US price erosion

blocks.p: Biocon Biologics sells 12 commercial biosimilars and has 20+ in development (Q1FY27 press release). Revenue grew from ₹8,818 cr in FY24 (incl. the India branded business sold in FY25) to ₹10,380 cr in FY26 (+16%; ~+7% in dollars per the CFO's rule of thumb that 3-4 points of rupee growth is currency) and ₹2,855 cr in Q1FY27 (+16%). EBITDA before other income went from ₹1,900 cr (21.3%) in FY25 to ₹2,566 cr (24.7%) in FY26 as North America's share rose and the Viatris integration costs fell away. The legacy portfolio is the cash engine: insulins above $300 mn a year, adalimumab above $250 mn, pegfilgrastim and trastuzumab ~$200 mn each and bevacizumab above $100 mn (CFO, Q4FY26 call).

blocks.h: The launches that matter for FY27-29

blocks.p: Management names five growth products: aflibercept, denosumab, aspart, ustekinumab and bevacizumab (CEO, Q1FY27 call). Three facts frame them. **Aflibercept** (Yesafili, eye injections for macular degeneration) launched in the US in August 2026 as an interchangeable biosimilar under a confidential settlement with the originator; one biosimilar already sells with a high share, which proves doctors will switch but also means Biocon is not first. **Denosumab** (Bosaya for osteoporosis in pharmacies, Aukelso for cancer in hospitals) launched in the US after the Q4FY26 close, behind several rivals. **Aspart** (Kirsty, the only interchangeable aspart in the US) is sold only in closed-door networks so far; the move to commercial formularies is planned for the second half of FY27. Ustekinumab (Yesintek) is the success story of FY26 (close to a fifth of the US biosimilar segment), and bevacizumab is being added in the US. July-September is when US payers sign contracts for the next calendar year; management says it is "in a good place" (Q1FY27 call).

Roughly 40% of biosimilar revenue is North America (46% in Q4FY26), 35% Europe (incl. Japan and Australia) and 25% emerging markets (CFO, Q4FY26 call). Europe is "very steady" and tender-led (adalimumab is the largest product there); North America carries the margin; emerging markets add volume (insulin shares above 50% in several countries, bevacizumab leadership in Brazil). Management guides to a "mid-20s" EBITDA margin rising with launches, and asks investors to normalise FY26's 27% (company basis) to 24-25% because Q3FY26 had an unusually North America-heavy allocation (Q1FY27 call). US price erosion is "real" and the company prefers margin to share.

blocks.p: Biocon's biosimilars are made in Bengaluru (monoclonal antibodies at Biocon Park and Biocon Campus, incl. the B3 and B5 drug-substance units) and Johor Bahru, Malaysia (insulins), with partner plants for adalimumab, etanercept and part of human insulin. sections.title: Generics: new plants, thin margins; profitable growth depends on utilisation and GLP-1s

blocks.p: The generics business sells APIs (about 60% of the segment in Q1FY27, two-thirds historically) and finished generics (pills from Cranbury, New Jersey and Bengaluru; injectables and peptides) in the US, Europe and emerging markets. External revenue was ₹2,859 cr in FY26 (+17% like for like after the one-time US lenalidomide sales of Q4FY25), but EBITDA before other income was only ₹43 cr (1.5%): new API plants at Vizag and Hyderabad, peptide and injectable capacity in Bengaluru and the Cranbury expansion carry costs before they carry volume ("margins reflect higher costs from recently commissioned facilities", Q4FY26 presentation). Gross margin is in the "early 40s" (CFO). Q1FY27 improved: revenue ₹760 cr (+21%), EBITDA ₹56 cr (7%, company basis), helped by API pricing premiums, R&D pruning and opex cuts after the integration (CFO, Q1FY27 call).

blocks.callout: **So what:** generics are worth little today (₹43 cr of FY26 EBITDA before other income) and their value in our SOTP (~₹23 a share at 9.5x Sep-28E EBITDA) assumes margins reach 9-11% as plants fill. That is plausible, since Q1FY27 is already at 7% on the company basis, but it is a recovery, not a franchise: API prices are set globally and Chinese competition is intense. The upside case is GLP-1 peptides, where fermentation-based capacity gives Biocon a cost edge.

sections.title: Syngene and Bicara: worth ~₹43 a share at market less 20%; both fell hard in 2025-26

blocks.p: **Syngene** is a contract research, development and manufacturing company with ~400 clients (BMS, GSK, Zoetis, Merck KGaA; the BMS partnership runs to 2035). FY26 revenue was ₹3,739 cr (+3%) with a 24.6% operating EBITDA margin. Then one large biologics client cut its offtake: Q1FY27 revenue fell 16% to ₹736 cr, the operating margin was 12% and Syngene lost ₹9 cr. Management calls FY27 a "transition year" with a single-digit rupee decline and a return to growth from FY28; Siddharth Mittal, Biocon's former CEO, now runs it (Q1FY27 call). Biocon owns 52.4% (AR FY26). At ₹365.3 on 30-Sep-2026 Syngene was worth ₹14,722 cr, so Biocon's stake was ₹7,714 cr, ₹47.3 a share. Syngene traded near ₹700 in 2024.

blocks.p: **Bicara Therapeutics** (Nasdaq: BCAX) is a US biotech developing ficerafusp alfa, a two-in-one antibody for head and neck cancer that has FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation (AR FY26). Biocon incubated it; its CEO is Claire Mazumdar, the chairperson's niece and named successor. Biocon holds 5,523,897 shares (AR FY26 note 5), ~10% of the company: at $18.61 on 30-Sep-2026 and ₹95.81/$, ₹985 cr (₹6.0 a share). The chairperson called it "no longer a significant investment" to be monetised "at the right time" (Q1FY27 call). Bicara's losses are not in Biocon's P&L (it is a fair-value investment), so no start-up losses need to be valued: its share price already reflects them.

Each ₹100 move in Syngene's share price changes our target by ~₹10. Selling down Syngene further (as Biocon did in FY23 and FY25) would turn the discount into cash and cut debt.

blocks.p: The best evidence of an advantage is durability: Biocon's US pegfilgrastim and trastuzumab still hold 20-25% shares seven and more years after launch, and its glargine is the only biosimilar insulin in the US. Those positions come from reliable supply of hard-to-make products, not from patents. The weakest evidence is returns: ROCE has been 4-6% since the Viatris deal, so the advantage has not yet covered the price paid for scale. Competition is getting stronger: Sandoz, Amgen, Celltrion, Samsung Bioepis, Teva/Alvotech and, in insulin, Chinese makers partnering with European companies (CEO, Q4FY26 call).

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** A narrow, real moat in biosimilar manufacturing and insulin, not in pricing. The returns record says the moat has not yet earned its cost of capital. It justifies valuing biosimilars at a premium to generics, not at a premium to the market.

sections.title: Revenue up 2.4x in five years; profit attributable to shareholders roughly halved

blocks.p: Biocon's consolidated revenue went from ₹7,143 cr in FY21 to ₹16,927 cr in FY26, 18.8% a year, mostly because Biocon Biologics bought Viatris's biosimilars business (closed 29-Nov-2022), which doubled the biosimilars segment. EBITDA before other income rose from ₹1,581 cr to ₹3,471 cr, but the margin slipped from 22.1% to 20.5%. Below EBITDA the deal's costs took everything: interest went from ₹58 cr to ₹990 cr and depreciation and amortisation from ₹715 cr to ₹1,957 cr. Profit attributable to shareholders fell from ₹740 cr to ₹386 cr, and per share from ₹6.2 to ₹2.4 once the shares issued since Jun-2025 (120 cr to 163 cr) are counted. FY24 and FY25 look better than they were: they carried ₹530 cr of Bicara gains and ₹1,057 cr from selling the India branded business.

What it has said: growth "to accelerate through the year" with a stronger second half; biosimilars margin "mid-20s" and rising; generics margins expanding; Syngene down single digits in rupees in FY27 and back to growth in FY28; lower capex; free cash to debt. MOSL reads the consolidated margin aspiration as ~24-25% on the company basis (incl. other income), which would be ~₹4,700 cr of company EBITDA on our FY27E revenue, against our ₹3,767 cr before other income (≈₹3,987 cr on the company basis). We think that aspiration needs both a fast launch ramp and a Syngene recovery in the same year.

sections.title: Returns on capital fell from 13% to 4%: a big, expensive bet still waiting to pay

blocks.p: Over FY21-26 Biocon generated ₹13,198 cr of operating cash and spent ₹11,584 cr on fixed assets (plants in Malaysia, Bengaluru, Vizag, Hyderabad and the US, plus Syngene's labs) and ₹449 cr on dividends; the Viatris deal (FY23, ~₹14,260 cr of investing outflow that year) was paid with debt and BBL shares. Equity raised: ₹4,500 cr (Jun-2025 QIP at ₹330) and ₹4,150 cr (Jan-2026 QIP at ₹368.35), plus 17.1 cr shares swapped to BBL's minorities. ROCE on Screener's basis fell from 13% in FY20 to 4% in FY26; ROE was 1.4%. Goodwill of ₹18,377 cr and other intangibles of ₹8,058 cr (Mar-26 balance sheet) are the price of the Viatris business; at a 10% pre-tax return they need ~₹2,600 cr a year of operating profit on their own.

sections.title: Earnings quality: one-offs in five of the last five years, other income inside "EBITDA", minorities until 2026

blocks.p: Four things a reader of Biocon's numbers should know. (1) **One-off gains and charges every year.** FY24 profit included a ₹530 cr gain on Bicara (dilution and fair value) and ₹350 cr from selling two branded units; FY25 a ₹1,057 cr gain on selling the India branded business and one-time US lenalidomide (~₹281 cr of EBITDA); FY26 ₹403 cr of pre-tax exceptional costs (integration, transaction, labour codes, inventory write-downs, a litigation settlement) partly offset by a ₹184 cr derivative gain. These gains sit in other income, not in "exceptional items", so Screener's profit before exceptional items still includes them. (2) **Company "EBITDA" includes other income** (FY26 ₹3,798 cr vs ₹3,471 cr before it); we forecast before other income. (3) **Minorities**: until January 2026 a quarter of BBL belonged to others, so consolidated profit overstated what shareholders earned (FY25: ₹1,429 cr before minorities, ₹1,013 cr after). (4) **Amortisation and capitalisation**: Biocon capitalises development costs (intangibles under development ₹2,392 cr at Jun-26) and borrowing costs on projects (Screener flags it), which flatters EBITDA today and raises amortisation later (D&A +20% YoY in Q1FY27).

The core of the debt is BBL's: $800 mn of 6.67% senior secured notes (callable from Oct-2026 at a premium) and a ~$295 mn syndicated loan, with term maturities moved out to FY29-30 (June-2026 presentation). blocks.p: Only three houses published after the Q1FY27 results that we could find by 30-Sep-2026: Motilal Oswal (Buy, ₹520, 6-Aug; SOTP with biosimilars at 22x EV/EBITDA, generics 10x, Syngene at market less 15%), BofA Securities (downgrade to Sell, ₹410, 10-Aug) and Axis Securities (Buy, ₹424, 19-Sep; SOTP). Older notes still standing include Nuvama (Buy, ₹480, SOTP: biosimilars 20x, generics 9x, Syngene 22x), JM Financial (Buy, ₹476, SOTP), Geojit (Accumulate, ₹439), ICICI Direct (Sell, ₹350), Citi (Sell, ₹360), ICICI Securities (Sell, ₹320) and Bernstein (Underperform, ₹326). The median of the 10 targets is ₹417, +13% vs the ₹370 close. Everyone who discloses a method uses a sum of the parts with biosimilars on EV/EBITDA; the disagreement is about the launch ramp and how much to pay for it. The stock fell from ₹437 before the Q1 results to ₹370 on 30-Sep-2026.

blocks.p: Every broker that discloses a method values Biocon as a sum of the parts: biosimilars and generics on EV/EBITDA, Syngene at its market value less a holding discount (MOSL 15%), sometimes Bicara. We do the same on Sep-28E EBITDA (half FY28E, half FY29E), deduct biopharma net debt at the same date and carry the result into the model as an implied P/E. Since BBL became wholly owned on 29-Jun-2026 there are no minorities left in the parts we value at 100%; Syngene's minorities are not deducted because we value only Biocon's 52.4%.

blocks.p: **Biosimilars: Biocon's own history, looked through.** BBL is not listed, but Biocon's share price has priced it every day. We strip out what else the market cap contains and divide by next year's biosimilars EBITDA: (Biocon's market value − 80% of its Syngene stake at market + net debt outside Syngene − generics at Aurobindo's forward multiple − FY25's one-time lenalidomide EBITDA) ÷ biosimilars EBITDA incl. corporate costs. Until January 2026 ~23-24% of BBL belonged to minorities, so both net debt and EBITDA are taken at Biocon's economic share (1 − m). The window starts in FY24 (1-Apr-2023): before the Viatris deal closed (Nov-2022) and Biocon sold down Syngene (70% to 55%), the share price valued a different company. On 183 weekly points the median is **19.4x** (25th-75th percentile 18.2-20.5x; FY24 18.9x, FY25 19.7x, FY26 19.9x, FY27 to date 20.0x) and **18.2x on 30-Sep-2026**. × the pharma EV/EBITDA factor (+7.46%) = 20.8x → **21x** (bull 22x, bear 19.5x from the 75th/25th percentiles). The street uses 20-22x.

**Generics: a stated peer basis.** Biocon's generics have no listed history of their own. The closest listed Indian peer is Aurobindo Pharma (vertically integrated API + US/EU formulations, low-to-mid margins). Its one-year-forward EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021 (EV = price × shares + latest published net debt; EBITDA = next full year, actuals then our published AUROPHARMA forecasts) has a median of **8.9x** (7.3-10.5x; 10.2x on 30-Sep-2026). × 1.0746 = 9.6x → **9.5x** (bull 11.5x, bear 8x). MOSL uses 10x, Nuvama 9x.

₹370: 40.9x Sep-28E EPS (expensive on earnings), ~18.2x forward EBITDA for biosimilars on our look-through (below its 19.4x median since FY24 and the street's 20-22x). Our SOTP gives {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}); the median of street targets is ₹417.

The upside comes from the rule: biosimilars valued on their own history plus listed stakes at market. FY26 removed the structural reasons for the discount (minorities, structured debt), and interest and capex are falling while the launches arrive.

Both cross-checks (EV/EBITDA ₹407, DCF ₹412 / ₹369 after minorities) sit near the price; our EPS is below the street; and the company has promised second-half acceleration before. blocks.callout: **How we would act:** buy in stages rather than all at once, with Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026) as the first checkpoint. The thesis is simple to monitor: biosimilars EBITDA has to move from ~₹730 cr a quarter towards ~₹900 cr through FY28 (our Sep-28E run-rate is ₹924 cr a quarter incl. corporate costs), and net debt has to fall. If both happen, 21x forward EBITDA gives the target; if the ramp stalls, the stock is worth roughly what it trades at.

exhibit.title: Terms used in this report
head: Term
What it means
rows: A biologic is a medicine made in living cells (insulin, antibodies). A biosimilar is an approved near-copy sold after the original's patents expire, usually 15-35% cheaper at launch.
A US designation allowing pharmacists to substitute the biosimilar for the original without asking the doctor (Biocon's glargine, aspart and aflibercept have it).
US drugs bought at pharmacies through insurers' formularies vs drugs given in clinics and hospitals and paid on average selling prices (ASP), which fall as competition rises.
A copy of an off-patent small-molecule drug; an API (active pharmaceutical ingredient) is the drug substance sold to other manufacturers.
Peptide drugs for diabetes and obesity (liraglutide, semaglutide); Biocon makes them by fermentation.
Contract research, development and manufacturing organisation: Syngene's business.

The US regulator; a Form 483 lists inspection observations; VAI ("voluntary action indicated") means cleared with fixes, OAI ("official action") is the bad outcome; a pre-licence inspection (PLI) precedes approval of a new biologic.
Qualified institutions placement: a share sale to institutional investors.
The part of a subsidiary owned by outside shareholders (Syngene's 47.6%; BBL's ~23% until Jan-2026).
Operating profit before depreciation, amortisation, interest, tax and other income (Screener basis); Biocon's own "EBITDA" includes other income.
Enterprise value (market value + net debt) divided by EBITDA; the street's yardstick for biosimilars and generics.
The multiple the market implicitly pays for one part of a group after subtracting the market value of its other parts.
Sum of the parts: each business valued separately, plus listed stakes, less net debt.
The twelve months to Sep-2028 (half FY28E + half FY29E): what the market will look at in Sep-2027, our target date.
Discounted cash flow; weighted average cost of capital (the blended cost of debt and equity).

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Biocon Ltd (consolidated, Rs crore; Net Profit on the attributable basis via tools/authoring/BIOCON.patch.js; 162.97 cr shares). Biocon Biologics (BBL, biosimilars) became wholly owned on 29-Jun-2026 (MOSL 6-Aug-2026; Q1FY27 press release); Syngene (research services, 52.4% owned, AR FY26 note 39) is consolidated. Revenue is Screener's revenue from operations; EBITDA is Screener's basis, i.e. BEFORE other income (Biocon's own 'EBITDA' includes other income: FY26 Rs3,798 cr vs Rs3,471 cr here). The business-line build (businessLines: biosimilars, generics, services on the AR FY26 note 40 external-revenue basis) and the segment EBITDA build are checked against model revenue and EBITDA in BIOCON.ctx.js. The engine has no minority line: Syngene's minorities (47.6%) are deducted inside otherIncome on a pre-tax-equivalent basis so that forecast EPS stays attributable (syngene block). Valuation: sum of the parts carried by BIOCON.sotp.js as an implied P/E on Sep-28E EPS.
assumptions._revenueWhy: From the business-line build (businessLines; the ctx script checks it within 0.3%). FY27E +11.4%: Q1FY27 revenue from operations +10% (biosimilars +16%, generics +21%, services -16%; Q1FY27 press release). About 8 points of the biosimilars and generics growth is the rupee: Biocon is 'largely a dollarized company' (CFO, Q4FY26 call) and the rupee averaged ~88.5/$ in FY26 vs ~94.7 in Q1FY27 and 95.81 at 30-Sep-2026 (PTI, as in SUNPHARMA). FY28E +11.6% and FY29E +10.0% at a flat rupee: full-year aflibercept, denosumab and aspart in the US, then slower. MOSL (6-Aug-2026) has Rs18,970 cr / Rs21,507 cr for FY27E / FY28E; Axis Securities (19-Sep-2026) Rs20,971 cr / Rs22,344 cr. We are in line with MOSL and 6-10% below Axis.

businessLines._why: FY26 external revenue by segment (AR FY26 note 40, Rs mn converted to Rs crore): biosimilars 10,379.8, generics 2,858.7, services (Syngene; 'CRDMO' until FY26) 3,688.5 = Rs16,927.0 cr. External revenue already nets inter-segment sales (FY26: generics sold Rs309 cr of API to the other segments). Growth in rupees. Biosimilars +17% / +13% / +10%: Q1FY27 +16% (Rs2,855 cr) of which ~10 points was the rupee (Q1FY26 ~85.6/$, Q1FY27 ~94.7/$), i.e. ~5% in constant currency; management guides to 'meaningful acceleration in the second half' (Q1 call) from Yesafili (aflibercept, US launch Aug-2026, interchangeable), Bosaya/Aukelso (denosumab, US launch May-2026), Kirsty (insulin aspart) moving to commercial US channels in 2HFY27 and the second Malaysia drug-product line (EMA-approved, supplying from Q2FY27). FY27E +17% = ~8% rupee + ~9% constant currency; FY28E +13% (full year of the launches, flat rupee; MOSL models a 16% FY26-28 CAGR to Rs14,000 cr, Nuvama ~21%); FY29E +10% (price erosion in the base portfolio, more aflibercept and denosumab competitors). Generics +16% / +12% / +10%: Q1FY27 +21% (Rs760 cr) with liraglutide 'in single digits' of the segment (Q1 call); FY26 +17% like for like; API is ~60% of the segment. Services (Syngene) -8% / +6% / +10%: Syngene guides to a single-digit rupee decline in FY27 after losing volume at a large biologics client (Q1: -16%), and a return to growth from FY28 (Q1 call); MOSL models a -3.4% FY26-28 CAGR.

Rs122.4 cr of other income), services Rs918.5 cr (24.9%), eliminations and unallocated -Rs72.1 cr; total Rs3,455 cr vs Screener Rs3,471 cr. FY25: biosimilars Rs1,900 cr (21.3%), generics Rs297 cr (10.8%, incl. one-time US lenalidomide), services Rs1,042 cr. Q1FY27 (company basis, incl. other income): biosimilars Rs728 cr (25%), generics Rs56 cr (7%), Syngene operating EBITDA margin 12%. Generics 6% / 9% / 11%: Q4FY26 8% and Q1FY27 7% on the company basis; gross margin 'early 40s'; new plants (Vizag, Hyderabad, Bengaluru peptides, Cranbury US) still under-used. Services 18% / 23% / 24.5% (Syngene operating EBITDA; FY26 24.6% on Syngene's own numbers, Q1FY27 12.4%; the company talks of a return to the mid-20s, which needs a much stronger second half). Syngene keeps investing (~Rs400-500 cr a year). MOSL models only Rs700 / 650 cr; we keep capitalised development and Syngene in, so Rs1,500 / 1,400 / 1,400 cr.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation and amortisation Rs1,957 cr = 4.4% of the average gross block (Screener: Rs40,804 cr to Rs48,079 cr; the block includes Rs18,377 cr of goodwill, which is not amortised, and jumped with the rupee). Q1FY27 D&A Rs548 cr (Rs2,192 cr annualised) and rising: launches move product intangibles out of 'under development' (Rs2,392 cr at Jun-26) and the Malaysia line is capitalised (CFO, Q1 call). 4.75% of the average block gives Rs2,319 / 2,388 / 2,455 cr (MOSL Rs2,297 / 2,499 cr). The engine holds CWIP flat (Rs6,987 cr incl. intangibles under development), which understates the step-up as those assets go live.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Not used: the engine applies the yield only to positive net cash, and Biocon has net debt (Screener basis Rs10,461 cr at Mar-26). Interest on Biocon's gross cash is built inside otherIncome instead.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built from sourced parts, then reduced by Syngene's minorities (the engine has no minority line). (1) Gross other income Rs220 / 230 / 240 cr: AR FY26 note 22 shows Rs342.5 cr in FY26 = interest on deposits Rs96.6 cr + other interest Rs18.8 cr + gains on current investments Rs83.7 cr + fair-value gains Rs79.5 cr + other non-operating income Rs63.9 cr; Q1FY27 was Rs55 cr (Rs80 cr a year earlier), i.e. ~Rs220 cr a year. We take interest at ~5.5% on ~Rs2,800 cr of cash and liquid investments (Rs2,833 cr at Jun-26: cash Rs1,518 cr + other bank balances Rs836 cr + current investments Rs479 cr) = ~Rs155 cr, plus ~Rs65-85 cr of fund gains and sundry income; no forex gains (none guided; the dollar debt is a natural hedge). (2) Less Syngene's minorities on a pre-tax-equivalent basis: 47.6% x Syngene profit (syngene block: Rs112 / 284 / 392 cr) = Rs54 / 135 / 187 cr after tax, grossed up at Biocon's tax rate = Rs65 / 173 / 242 cr. Result: Rs155 / 57 / -2 cr (the ctx script rebuilds it and checks it within Rs3 cr). BBL has no minorities from 29-Jun-2026 (Q1FY27 minorities were a net credit of Rs4 cr, Syngene's share of its loss).
assumptions._interestLabel: Finance costs (BBL's $800 mn 6.67% notes and syndicated loan, working-capital debt, leases, Syngene)
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs990 cr (Screener; Q1FY26 Rs277 cr falling to Rs213 cr in Q1FY27 after the structured instruments were redeemed with the June-2025 QIP: ~Rs300 cr a year of savings, CFO Q4FY26 call). Gross debt Rs15,551 cr at Jun-26 incl. Rs598 cr of leases (balance sheet), ~5.5% average cost (Q1 annualised Rs852 cr). Rs820 / 745 / 630 cr = 5.5% on our own average gross-debt path: Rs15,434 cr at Mar-26 falling to ~Rs10,300 cr at Mar-29 as free cash goes to debt (CFO); the path is the model's net debt plus the working capital the engine misses, with cash held at Mar-26 levels. BIOCON.ctx.js rebuilds it and checks it within 5%. The $800 mn notes are callable from Oct-2026 at a premium; we assume no refinancing.
assumptions._taxWhy: Effective tax rate before exceptional items 21% in FY26 and 23% in FY25 (Board's report, AR FY26); Q1FY27 had a credit (tax -Rs6 cr on PBT Rs141 cr, MOSL: 'tax benefit'). FY27E 18% (Q1 credit plus ~22% for the rest of the year), then 22% and 23% (MOSL 19.1% / 21.0%). The engine taxes the pre-tax minority deduction at the same rate, which keeps PAT attributable.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Dividend Rs0.50 a share for FY25 and FY26 (Rs81 cr, ~21% of FY26 attributable profit; AR FY26). Free cash goes to debt reduction first (CFO, Q4FY26 and Q1FY27 calls). 12% / 10% / 10% keeps the dividend around Rs0.50-1.0.

syngene._why: Syngene's own P&L, used only for the minority deduction (the stake itself is valued at market in the SOTP). Base FY26 (Syngene, Screener consolidated): revenue Rs3,739 cr, operating EBITDA Rs921 cr (24.6%), D&A Rs453 cr, interest Rs49 cr, other income -Rs9 cr (hedge losses), net profit Rs317 cr; Q1FY27 revenue Rs736 cr, EBITDA Rs91 cr, loss Rs9 cr. Revenue growth and margin as in businessLines (services); D&A Rs470 / 490 / 510 cr (FY26 Rs453 cr plus new ADC and biologics capacity); interest Rs45 / 40 / 35 cr (Rs458 cr of debt incl. Rs449 cr leases at Mar-26); other income Rs40 / 55 / 65 cr (Rs1,574 cr of cash and investments at Mar-26, less hedge losses in FY27); tax 22%. Biocon's stake 52.4% (AR FY26 note 39), minorities 47.6%.

sotp._why: Written by tools/authoring/BIOCON.sotp.js from BIOCON.ctx.js (derived multiples and the parts per case). Do not edit by hand.

dcf._betaWhy: The engine discounts at the cost of equity (PLAYBOOK §7); beta 0.72 gives 10.8%, our WACC: market value Rs60,348 cr at Rs370.3, gross debt Rs15,551 cr at Jun-26 (20% of capital) at ~5.5% pre-tax (4.3% after tax), cost of equity ~12.5% at beta 1.0 for a leveraged, US-exposed biosimilars company.
dcf._tgWhy: 5% nominal: biosimilar volumes grow with biologic loss-of-exclusivity waves (~$200 bn of biologic sales lose protection over the next decade, company presentations) but prices fall every year; insulin and oncology are mature.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~10% in FY29E to 7% by year 15.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 24%: roughly the FY29E consolidated margin held; launches offset price erosion, Syngene recovers to the mid-20s.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: 5.5% of revenue (FY26 ~11% in the investment phase; FY27-29E ~6-8%).
dcf._depWhy: 8% of revenue = the tax-deductible D&A in the long run (FY26 book D&A 11.6% of revenue incl. amortisation of the acquired Viatris intangibles, which runs off).
dcf._minorityNote: The engine's DCF values 100% of Syngene's cash flows and does not deduct Syngene's minorities; the report shows the DCF less 47.6% of Syngene at market as well.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Yesafili (aflibercept) and Bosaya/Aukelso (denosumab) take meaningful US share before most rivals arrive, Kirsty (aspart) wins commercial formularies, the second Malaysia line fills, the FDA's lighter biosimilar rules cut development costs by half as management says, Syngene recovers to mid-20s margins in FY28, and liraglutide/GLP-1 peptides lift generics margins into the teens.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: US price erosion accelerates as Chinese and Korean biosimilars and new entrants crowd aflibercept, denosumab and ustekinumab; insulin share gains stall; a US tariff or an FDA action on a Bengaluru or Malaysia site interrupts supply; generics plants stay under-used; Syngene's lost biologics volume is not replaced.

methods.name: Sum of the parts (implied P/E)
methods.why: How the street values Biocon: a sum of the parts (MOSL 6-Aug-2026: biosimilars 22x EV/EBITDA, generics 10x, Syngene at market less 15%; Axis Securities 19-Sep-2026 and Nuvama, JM Financial earlier: SOTP). Biosimilars 21x Sep-28E EBITDA = Biocon's own look-through one-year-forward EV/EBITDA for the business since Apr-2023 (median 19.4x on 183 weekly points: market value less the Syngene stake at market less 20%, plus net debt, less generics at Aurobindo's forward median, with BBL's minorities taken pro rata) x the pharma EV/EBITDA factor of +7.46% (nine-name set; Biocon is outside it; PLAYBOOK §7c), rounded to the half-turn. Generics 9.5x = Aurobindo's forward EV/EBITDA median since Apr-2021 (8.9x) x the same factor (stated peer basis: no own history). Less biopharma net debt at Sep-28E; plus 52.4% of Syngene and the Bicara stake at 30-Sep market value less 20% (house precedent; MOSL uses 15%). No minorities left in parts valued at 100% (BBL wholly owned from 29-Jun-2026). Sum Rs485 a share = 53.62x Sep-28E EPS (Rs9.1). Bull 22x / 11.5x (75th percentiles) on bull EBITDA => 47.89x; bear 19.5x / 8x (25th percentiles) on bear EBITDA => 71.58x.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA (consolidated)
methods.why: Consolidated, on Biocon's own history: 14.5x Sep-28E EBITDA = the 17.6x median trailing EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021 (Screener, EBITDA incl. other income) x the +7.46% factor, restated from the twelve months to Jun-26 (Rs3,854 cr incl. other income) to Sep-28E EBITDA before other income (Rs4,987 cr). Bull 18x and bear 11x use the 75th and 25th percentiles. The history counts 100% of EBITDA but leaves BBL's minorities (23-24% until Jan-2026) out of EV, so it understates the multiple.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether consolidated cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF at 10.8% (beta set so the cost of equity equals our WACC), terminal growth 5%, plus the model's net debt at Mar-27E. It counts 100% of Syngene; the report also shows it less Syngene's minorities at market.
